{
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.5,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R100"],
      "pins": ["R100.1", "R100.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R100 is valued \"24k\" on an 0805 footprint, but its library description and MPN (FRC0805J240TSD) describe a 24Ω ±5% chip resistor. The value field disagrees with the part's own metadata.",
      "expected": "A 24Ω resistor between VOUTN and VOUTP, consistent with its 24Ω ±5% description and the 24Ω MPN.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(ref \"R100\") (value \"24k\") (footprint \"Resistor_SMD:R_0805_2012Metric\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(description \" 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(property (name \"MPN\") (value \"FRC0805J240TSD\"))"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R100 VOUTN VOUTP 24k"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the board was built with 24kΩ instead of 24Ω, the element across the PoE output (VOUTN/VOUTP) behaves very differently: it draws only a tiny bleed current rather than acting as the intended low-value load/damping element, so the output network will not behave as designed.",
      "confidence": 0.5
    },
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["D34", "D35", "D40"],
      "pins": ["D34.2", "D35.2", "D40.2"],
      "nets": ["/NET0048"],
      "observed": "The anodes of three LEDs (D34, D35, D40) sit on a net named /NET0048 that contains only those three anode pins. No supply rail or other connection is present on that net. Each LED's cathode goes to a status line through a series resistor (R45, R57, R87 to nLED2, PI_nLED_Activity and nLED3).",
      "expected": "Status LED anodes should return to the +3V3 rail, as the other status LEDs do (e.g., D16 and D25 have their anodes on +3V3), so that the active-low CM4 LED outputs can light them.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"15\") (name \"/NET0048\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"D34\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D35\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D40\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"+3V3\") ... (node (ref \"D16\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "The three Ethernet/activity status LEDs have no supply path on their anodes, so they will never light, removing the network activity and link indication they were meant to give.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The strongest deviation is R100, whose value of 24k contradicts its 24Ω library description and MPN. A weaker candidate is that three status LED anodes are floating on an isolated net with no supply connection. Several spec-to-netlist mismatches (such as U5/U15/SW1 references) look like spec drift and were not reported.",
  "summary_note": "Confidence is moderate; the spec appears to describe a different revision in several places, so those were not treated as anomalies."
}

anomalies.observed: R100 is valued "24k" on an 0805 footprint, but its library description and MPN (FRC0805J240TSD) describe a 24Ω ±5% chip resistor. The value field disagrees with the part's own metadata.
anomalies.expected: A 24Ω resistor between VOUTN and VOUTP, consistent with its 24Ω ±5% description and the 24Ω MPN.

evidence.quote: (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: If the board was built with 24kΩ instead of 24Ω, the element across the PoE output (VOUTN/VOUTP) behaves very differently: it draws only a tiny bleed current rather than acting as the intended low-value load/damping element, so the output network will not behave as designed.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of three LEDs (D34, D35, D40) sit on a net named /NET0048 that contains only those three anode pins. No supply rail or other connection is present on that net. Each LED's cathode goes to a status line through a series resistor (R45, R57, R87 to nLED2, PI_nLED_Activity and nLED3).
anomalies.expected: Status LED anodes should return to the +3V3 rail, as the other status LEDs do (e.g., D16 and D25 have their anodes on +3V3), so that the active-low CM4 LED outputs can light them.
anomalies.impact: The three Ethernet/activity status LEDs have no supply path on their anodes, so they will never light, removing the network activity and link indication they were meant to give.

A weaker candidate is that three status LED anodes are floating on an isolated net with no supply connection.
